s01.setup: A ferry carrying the harbour's lamp oil has stalled at the dock, and a crowd is waiting on the quay.
s01.line: That engine has not purred like that in years.
s01.lit: The oil is ashore and the harbour lamp catches. The water glows back.

o.R: Open the ferry's engine and fix what is broken
o.I: Track the tides and wind to work out why it stalled
o.A: Paint a bright welcome board for the waiting crowd
o.S: Sing with the waiting children so they stay calm

s02.setup: The old stone bridge has a cracked arch, and lantern-bearers need to cross before midnight.
s02.line: My father laid that arch. It is good to see it lit again.
s02.lit: Lantern-bearers stream across, and the old arch glows.

o.R: Fit the new planks exactly as the plan shows
o.I: Find out how old arches stay up, and why this one cracked
o.A: Imagine a bridge shape unlike any other
o.E: Take charge of the budget and the team for the repair

s03.setup: The tower clock that tells the lane when to light its lamps has gone wrong.
s03.line: Right on dusk, and the whole lane is ready.
s03.lit: The tower strikes dusk. Every window in the lane lights at once.

o.R: Climb the tower and follow the broken gear by hand
o.I: Study the pattern of missed chimes to find the cause
o.A: Decorate the clock face with something that makes people smile
o.C: Start a repair log and list who does which job

s04.setup: Apples are ripening faster than the village can press them.
s04.line: Sweet air, sweet juice, and now a lamp. A good evening's work.
s04.lit: The orchard is calm. Its lamp swings among the apple trees.

o.R: Run the press and keep it humming all day
o.I: Mix apple blends to discover a new juice flavour
o.S: Teach visiting children to make juice through games
o.E: Sell the juice and keep track of the money

s05.setup: Fog has settled on the mountain pass, the signal lamp is dim, and travellers are feeling their way through.
s05.line: Nobody was left behind in my pass tonight.
s05.lit: A thin gold line cuts the fog. The pass has its light, and the way is clear.

o.R: Mend the signal lamp so travellers can see it
o.I: Map where the fog is thickest and find out why
o.S: Welcome the lost travellers and get them moving together
o.C: Count everyone through the pass and keep the line in order

s06.setup: The bazaar opens at dusk. Your borrowed stall is empty, apart from a strange old machine in the corner.
s06.line: A lit lamp is the best sign a stall can have.
s06.lit: The bazaar glows, and a lamp hangs overhead, warm as a cup of tea.

o.R: Build a sturdy stall frame from the plan
o.I: Examine the strange old machine and work out what it was for
o.E: Call out to the crowd and make every visitor feel welcome
o.C: Sort the stock by size and label every shelf

s07.setup: A wide river blocks the road, and tired lamp-bearers have stopped to rest on the bank.
s07.line: The river will carry your lamp's light all the way to the sea.
s07.lit: The group is rested and ready for the crossing. The lamp's reflection drifts downstream.

o.R: Build a raft and test which wood floats best
o.A: Sketch a boat unlike any you have seen
o.S: Look after the tired travellers and help them get going again
o.E: Lead the camp meeting and make sure everyone is heard

s08.setup: The great loom that weaves the banners is creaking, and market day is near.
s08.line: Every banner in town will glow a little brighter tomorrow.
s08.lit: Banners hang above the street, and a lamp lights behind them.

o.R: Repair the loom so it runs smoothly again
o.A: Design a pattern that tells the town's story
o.S: Coach a shy weaver to show their work with pride
o.C: Check every roll of cloth and store it in order

s09.setup: A group needs to reach the cliff top by evening, and the glassy rock is glowing strangely.
s09.line: From up here the whole road looks like a string of stars.
s09.lit: The highest lamp is lit. The cliffs shine like glass for miles.

o.R: Rope down the cliff and test the rock as you go
o.A: Sit and watch the cliff light shift, and capture it in a drawing
o.E: Split the climbers into teams and set the timetable
o.C: Check every harness and rope, then brief everyone on the plan

s10.setup: A load of salt has spilled, two traders are arguing, and a crowd is gathering.
s10.line: Quiet market, warm lamp. The best kind of night.
s10.lit: The market hums, and its lamp is lit above the stalls.

o.R: Haul the barrels and stack them so they stay put
o.S: Help a lost trader find their family and rally others to help
o.E: Settle the argument with a deal both traders accept
o.C: Weigh and record every sack, then pack the cart

s11.setup: A clear night is coming, and visitors are climbing the hill to watch the stars come out.
s11.line: The sky has been waiting for this.
s11.lit: The hill lamp lifts its light into the dark, and the sky answers.

o.I: Chart the stars and wonder what is out there
o.A: Paint the night sky and notice how it changes
o.S: Show visitors around and invite them to join the stargazing club
o.E: Run the club night and make sure everyone is included

s12.setup: The garden that grows the sweet lamp-herbs is overgrown, and the season is turning.
s12.line: The herbs will sleep well tonight.
s12.lit: The beds breathe, and the lamp smells of rain and mint.

o.I: Test soils and seeds to grow healthier plants
o.A: Shape the garden so it feels peaceful to walk in
o.S: Teach children to care for the plants through stories
o.C: Label every herb and keep the beds in tidy rows

s13.setup: An old printing press has been found in a cellar, and the whole quarter wants it working.
s13.line: Ink and light. They go together.
s13.lit: Ink and paper fill the quarter, and a lamp lights above the cellar door.

o.I: Investigate how the old press makes its mark
o.A: Design a new letter style and see if people can read it
o.E: Pitch a new newspaper, with a plan and a price
o.C: Proofread every page and keep the print run on time

s14.setup: Travellers have come to rest before the next leg of the road, and some are unwell tonight.
s14.line: Steady light. They can rest now.
s14.lit: The house settles into calm. A steady lamp burns in the window.

o.I: Test the water supply to find what is making people ill
o.S: Comfort the patients and organise helpers for the night
o.E: Run the front desk so everyone is seen kindly and in turn
o.C: Count the medicine store and put it in perfect order

s15.setup: The square where all the lamps will gather is still bare, and the festival begins at dusk.
s15.line: All the lamps are lit. Let the festival begin!
s15.lit: The square is ready, and its lamp glows over the cobbles.

o.A: Create the welcome arch with a story in its design
o.S: Perform with the visitors so everyone feels part of it
o.E: Run the festival: the stalls, the prices and the plan
o.C: Keep the permits and timings in order, and keep stallholders informed

chapters.title: The Road Wakes
chapters.line: The first lamps are the hardest. Light a few, and the road starts to remember itself.

chapters.title: Hills and Rivers
chapters.line: The road climbs and bends. Somewhere ahead, a girl with a ferry lantern is looking for the lighthouse too.

chapters.title: The Salt Wind
chapters.line: You can smell the sea. The lighthouse is close, and so is the last piece of the note.

ila.3: Ahead on the road, a girl with a ferry lantern waves. "I am Ila. I saw your lamp from the water."
ila.6: Ila catches up, carrying a flask of lamp oil. "The lighthouse needs this. Walk with me a while."
ila.9: Ila points past the hills to the dark sea. "The lighthouse. Look how dark it still is."
ila.12: Ila hands you her lantern. "Almost there. Whatever you carry, it is enough."
